key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, reducing porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak hardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the O2/C2H2 ratio offers a practical process-control lever to optimize coating quality for wear- and corrosion-resistant surface engineering on stainless steel substrates.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied oxygen-to-acetylene ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, adhesion rising from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, and maximum microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: The optimal gas ratio may depend on spray distance, feedstock state, and part geometry, so the reported trends should be validated for other setups before scale-up.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
